title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U is a smooth K-variety (in the Longue Marche context, typically a moduli space of curves) with a compactification X whose boundary is a divisor with normal crossings and components D_i. For J a set of indices, D_J is the corresponding stratum and X_J a henselian/tubular neighbourhood of it. U_J = X_J ∩ U is the 'punctured tubular neighbourhood'. Heuristically U_J is homotopic to a (Ĝ_m)^J-torus fibration over D_J. Its fibre has π_1 equal to the inertia torus T^J ≅ Ẑ(1)^J. L̄ ⊃ K̄ are the chosen universal covers / base points. The E^{L̄}_U are the arithmetic fundamental groups: extensions of E^{K̄}_K = Gal(K̄/K) by the geometric group π^{L̄}_{U/K}.

Previous page. Grothendieck feared the boundary map π_2(D_J) → π_1(fibre) = T^J might be non-zero; topologically it is the Chern-class obstruction of the normal bundle. He maps the homotopy sequence of U_J → X_J ~ D_J to that of U → Spec K. Since π_2(Spec K) = 0, the composite π_2(D_J) → T^J → π_{U/K} vanishes. So if T^J → π_{U/K} is injective, π_2(D_J) → T^J is zero.

This page. He therefore admits that (37) gives an honest extension. This yields a morphism of short exact sequences (38):
1 → T^J → E^{L̄}_{U_{J,α}} → E^{D̃}_{D_{J,α}} → 1
mapping to
1 → π^{L̄}_{U/K} → E^{L̄}_U → E^{K̄}_K → 1.
He corrects himself: (37) only makes sense when D_J (equivalently X_J) is connected. In general one works one connected component X_{J,α}, D_{J,α}, U_{J,α} at a time. He notes that the intrinsic formulation is via multiplicative types and fundamental groupoids. Choosing a point x ∈ D_J gives homomorphisms (39) T^J → π^{L̄}_{U/K}. Each is defined only up to inner automorphisms of E^{L̄}_U by elements whose image in Gal(K̄/K) lies in the image of Gal(k(x)^-/k(x)).

Next page. For x in a fixed component D_{J,α} these are all conjugate; for J = {i} one gets the inertia homomorphisms κ_i : T → π_{U/K}. These are outer homomorphisms compatible with the outer Galois actions on T (cyclotomic) and on π_{U/K}.

Purpose. This is the general machinery for the 'divisors at infinity' of moduli spaces M_{g,n}. Inertia at boundary strata gives the Dehn-twist subgroups and the Galois-equivariant gluing data of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The exactness on the left of the top row of (38) is only 'admitted'. It rests on injectivity of T^J → π^{L̄}_{U/K}, which is assumed, not proved. For the moduli of curves this is the profinite injectivity of free abelian groups generated by Dehn twists along disjoint curves, a non-trivial fact proved much later. In general (e.g. U = A^2 in P^2) it fails, and π_2(D_J) → T^J can be non-zero: it is the Chern-class/Euler obstruction of the normal bundle.

Two points are heuristic rather than rigorous: the homotopy equivalence D_J ~ X_J and the torus-bundle picture of U_J in étale homotopy. They are fine for the open stratum in the tame/henselian setting (Grothendieck–Murre), but are used without proof here.

ideas.what: Punctured tubular neighbourhood U_J of a normal-crossing stratum as a torus fibration over D_J, giving the extension 1 → T^J → π_1(U_J) → π_1(D_J) → 1, with T^J = Ẑ(1)^J tame inertia
ideas.modern_name: Tame / logarithmic fundamental group of a normal crossings neighbourhood; local monodromy torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (LNM 208, 1971), SGA1 XIII; later log-geometry (Kato–Nakayama, Illusie, Vidal)

ideas.what: Vanishing of π_2(D_J) → T^J deduced from injectivity of the inertia torus into the geometric fundamental group of U, by comparing with the homotopy sequence over Spec K
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of local and global homotopy sequences; K(π,1)/good-neighbourhood arguments
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in anabelian / profinite Teichmüller literature (Nakamura, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: possibly in the Malgoire edition of La Longue Marche (1995)

ideas.what: Inertia homomorphisms κ_i : T → π_{U/K}, defined up to inner automorphisms by elements over Gal(k(x)), conjugate along a connected component of D_J, giving outer homomorphisms equivariant for the outer Galois actions; intrinsic version via fundamental groupoids and multiplicative types
ideas.modern_name: Galois-equivariant inertia (Dehn twist) subgroups at the boundary of M_{g,n}; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); Ihara, Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (sketch); La Longue Marche (Malgoire ed.)

missed.claim: A clean diagnosis is made explicit: the potential obstruction to the inertia extension (the boundary map π_2(D_J) → T^J, i.e. a normal-bundle Chern-class term) is killed by injectivity of inertia into the global geometric π_1. It is a small but explicit criterion, not a new result.
missed.quote: On va donc admettre que (37) définit bien une structure d'extensions, et on aura un tour de suites exactes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It slightly documents Grothendieck's awareness, around 1981, of the issue later handled by profinite Dehn-twist injectivity results (Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki). It is of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard working-out of tame inertia at normal-crossing boundary strata and of the outer inertia homomorphisms. The content is well known from Grothendieck–Murre and later anabelian work, and largely anticipated in Esquisse/Longue Marche. The only mildly notable point is the explicit π_2 worry and its conditional resolution.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 of the text probably reads 'Pour bien rectifier le tir, en faisant abstraction du fait que (37) n'a de sens telle quelle que si D_J est connexe' rather than 'Pour bien vérifier la chose, on fait abstraction que'.
End of page: '... automorphismes intérieurs des E^{L̄}_U, induits par [éléments dont l'image dans E_K^{K̄} est ...]', continuing on the next page.
The crossed-out label '(38?)' sits beside the top row; the final label (38) is beside the bottom row of the diagram.
